hypothesis: The project's hypothesis: a capability leaves a recurring difference between the traces of correct and wrong answers, and editing the weights where that recurring difference lives repairs the capability. This run tests no part of it. It asks two questions of the instrument every step of a correction loop pays for: whether the recorder writes each answer's files with the bytes it writes today when several engine contexts compute at once on the card as threads of one process, and whether the thirty answers of a capture would then come sooner.
why_this_direction: Steps 1 and 2 of the method are the overlaps of the full traces, and step 5 measures the computation again on the current model's own answers after every update: each such measurement is the engine's capture of the thirty fitting answers, and under Astra's choice of November 15 that capture is the measured loss at every step. With the kept scheduler adopted (controlled-bf16-8) the generation is still the largest part of a step: about 154 s of about 222 s before the write, as arithmetic. Inside it, three measurements say where the time is not (the recorder's bookkeeping, the waits for the card, processes side by side) and one says where a quarter of it was (the number of graph launches a compute). What is left to one context is that the card stands idle while that context's one processor thread prepares the next token, hashes the scores and writes the kept outputs: in recorder-kept-original the card's sampled utilization had medians of 37 to 44 on the installed side and 43 to 60 on the kept side. A second context could use that time only if the card does not have to switch to serve it: recorders-beside-original's processes each had a context of their own on the card and were slower; threads of one process share one. That difference is the one thing this run changes, and it is the next step because it is the last arrangement of the existing computation that has not been measured; going further (several answers sharing one read of the weights in one decode) changes kernels and is a different computation.
repeating_pattern_check: Four things have happened more than once. (1) A faster way to read turned out to be another computation: thirty-two tokens at once, the second card, the torch forward. Why: the kernels or their order differed. Here each context computes each token by the installed kernels in the installed order with fusion off; what is new is that two or three do so at the same time on one card, sharing its memory pool and its math library's handles. Whether that leaves the bytes alone is not argued here: every answer's four files are compared by sha256 in every arrangement, and the prediction on bytes is held with less confidence than the two schedulers' were. (2) A lever priced from a sample was not the cost: the bookkeeping (2.2 to 2.4 ms of a token), the 212 waits (4%), processes beside (0.72). Why: the price came from one sample of where the time seemed to be. Here the range predicted includes no gain and a loss, the workers recorder with one worker is measured as its own baseline in the same hold of the lock, and the engine's own phase timers are read on both schedulers so a result has its reason beside it. (3) A timing was taken on a loaded machine and its quiet-machine value is not known (recorder-kept-original: load average 21 to 28, another process on card 0 in one call). This run cannot quiet the machine (the load is other projects'; it was about 20 at 8:32 AM CT). It records the load average and the card's other processes with every arrangement, the arrangements follow one another under one hold, and what is reported is each arrangement over the one-worker arrangement of the same run, with the load beside it. (4) My own pages said one library differs on the kept side when two do (found at 8:14 AM CT, corrected). This declaration says what each arrangement loads from the loader's own trace, and says what the comparison does not read.
what_went_wrong_before: Every construction so far repaired some answers and broke others, and the repeated correction on state values was stopped in its first pass. A step of a loop was 1 h 35 to 2 h in the on-policy loop and 44 to 52 minutes as the stopped loop's launcher stood; Marcos expects minutes. Under the gradient step Astra specified the capture is the largest part of a step. Of the four measured attempts at its generation, two recorder processes beside each other were slower, reading the outputs back once a split gained 4%, and computing a split as one graph gained a quarter and is adopted; the bookkeeping was measured on the processor and is not a factor. None of them used the card's idle time between one context's tokens.
rule: Data roles: the first ten of the thirty fitting answers of the cohort controlled-bf16-1 (tube.picks, in the selection's order: own_text.py's first call) and no others. The answers no fit uses are not generated, read or listed; the reserved folder is not opened. The model is the original file, read only. One step (`compare`), under one hold of card 0's lock, seven arrangements in this order, each generating the same ten answers from their prompts alone as own_text.py asks for them: installed; workers-1; workers-2; workers-3; workers-3-kept; installed-timed; kept-timed. Before every arrangement each program, library and file of the comparison is hashed and held to this declaration; a process's scheduler library is held by the file and inode its own map shows and by the scheduler's own line in its log; an arrangement that fails either ends the comparison. Each answer's four files (stream.f32, stream.jsonl, result.json, case.json) are compared by sha256 with the installed arrangement's. An arrangement's record is written before anything of it is removed; streams whose files are the installed bytes are removed, and an answer with one file apart keeps its streams and the installed arrangement's whole. The seconds are the recorder's own (the workers recorder says them on its error stream; the installed recorder's are read from its files' times as in the earlier comparisons); the two timed arrangements' seconds enter no comparison of time. Nothing measured here starts, stops or selects anything. No instrument and no protocol is changed by this run: a capture through a workers recorder would be a separate acceptance, with its own protocol.

prediction.1_bytes: 10 of 10 answers' four files have the installed arrangement's sha256 in every arrangement. For workers-1 and the two timed arrangements this is held as firmly as the earlier comparisons' results (one context at a time, the installed or the qualified kept scheduler). For two and three workers it is held with less confidence than any earlier prediction of bytes here: nothing in the engine's sources I read shares mutable state between contexts of one model (the card backend keeps its state by context and guards what is shared), but concurrent contexts on one card have not been run by this project, and a memory pool or a math-library handle shared between them is where bytes could move.
prediction.2_time: workers-1 writes the answers at the installed recorder's rate (the same program path; within what two back-to-back calls differ by on this machine, which recorder-kept-original's calls put at tens of percent under load). With two and three workers the steps a second over one worker lie between 0.7 (what processes beside each other gave) and about 2.3 (one over the card's sampled utilization with one context, 0.43 to 0.60 on the kept side and 0.37 to 0.44 on the installed side): the bounds come from those two records, and no value inside them is predicted, because no measurement here says how much of a token's host time can overlap another context's card time. On the kept scheduler three workers are expected to gain less over one than on the installed one, since its card is busier.
prediction.3_card_and_phases: the card holds the weights once: three workers hold under 1 GB more than one (a recorder with one context holds about 5.05 GB, 4.38 of it the weights; the kept scheduler 0.6 to 1.0 GB more). The engine's phase timer attributes most of a decode call's host time to graph_compute on the installed scheduler and less of it on the kept one; its statics are shared between threads without a lock, so it is read only on the two one-context timed arrangements.
prediction.time_denominators: the workers recorder's steps a second count every case of the call over the seconds its own line states, which begin before the contexts are made; the installed recorder's milliseconds a step count each case from the end of the case before it, so the call's first case and the start are left out. They are different intervals over different cases: ratios between worker counts use the workers recorder's one definition, and the two are never divided by each other (workers.json carries this as `denominators`).

would_weaken_it: Nothing here bears on the hypothesis. On the instrument: (1) one file of one answer with other bytes in an arrangement of two or three workers means contexts computing at once on one card are another computation as far as the record goes: the variant is closed whatever its time, both streams are kept and the labels that differ say where. (2) Other bytes with ONE worker would mean the edits changed the program, which they must not: the workers recorder is then not the installed recorder and nothing of its timing is used. (3) No more steps a second with two or three workers than with one, or fewer, means the card's idle time between one context's tokens is not available to another context this way; the lever is closed and the record says what the phase timers show. (4) A crash, a hang or a refused context with several workers is recorded as it stands; the comparison ends there and what ran before it is kept.
inputs_read_for_what: The model is read by the recorders and never written. The cohort's declaration, the registered membership, the inputs' index and the wide overlap's members give the fitting answers, their prompts' tokens and their limits (ladder.cohort, tube.picks, cases.chosen), as own_text.py takes them. The instruments (the two recorders, the patch and its generator, the kept library, the comparison and the three files it imports from) are named under implementation with their sha256.

faster.derivation: steps a second of an arrangement: the steps of its ten answers over the recorder's own seconds from its workers' start to its last case's end (the workers recorder says them; for the installed recorder, each answer's seconds from the end of the answer before it, as recorder_kept.py reads them). Reported: each arrangement's steps a second, each over the one-worker arrangement's, the milliseconds a step, the card's memory at its most, the load average. A measurement, not a gate: no value of it starts or stops anything

One context only, because the phase timer's counters are shared between threads without a lock
